title: Sonar and parking sensors
body: A research ship is mapping the sea floor. Its sonar sends short pulses of ultrasonic waves straight down into the seawater and records the time after which the reflected pulse returns to the ship. The speed of sound in this seawater is taken as 1500 m s-1. Back on land, one of the scientists drives a car fitted with an ultrasonic parking sensor. The sensor sends ultrasonic waves of about 40 kHz towards obstacles behind the car and measures how long the reflected waves take to return; the speed of these waves in air is taken as 340 m s-1. In both devices the wave travels to the reflecting object and back, so the measured time is for a round trip.
